title: Opaque variant swap to incompatible tokenizer during capacity reconciliation
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: During a routine capacity reconciliation window in EU-West, the smart-routing compatibility resolver selected a quantized legacy variant that used a different tokenizer schema than the customer-bound model. This produced garbled outputs and increased 5xx / malformed-response errors for three enterprise tenants for ~22 minutes. Root cause: a race between the policy-refresh job and capacity-tag reconciliation allowed an interim routing decision to consult an out-of-date variant-compatibility cache. The compatibility resolver then fell back to the first available 'compatible' variant by tag without validating tokenizer contract (tokenizer_version mismatch). Incident magnitude: affected customers experienced high error rates and a latency spike; support escalations opened (SUP-7821, SUP-7823, SUP-7829). Immediate mitigations included: emergency rollback of the policy rollout, a temporary capacity-tag override to pin affected tenants to known-good variants, and a targeted route-blacklist to prevent the legacy variant from being chosen. Permanent fix: change compatibility resolver to enforce tokenizer/payload contract checks, add atomic reconciliation barrier during policy refresh, and increase variant TTL semantics to avoid mid-evaluation staleness.

2025-02-18: 09:10 UTC - Investigation: discovered compatibility-cache returned stale entry due to TTL miscalculation combined with parallel reconcile job. Compatibility resolver did not verify tokenizer_version field before selecting fallback.
